active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on capacity-safe GPU slots with exact marginal KVPR costs
active_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a pressure-aware greedy assignment, then only accepts strictly lexicographically improving single moves or swaps; this is good at preserving feasibility but is easily trapped when several models must move simultaneously. Replace the initial greedy choice on small and medium instances with one global bipartite assignment call using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Build a fixed number of capacity-safe slots per GPU, where a slot represents an allowed memory band and is only eligible for models whose size fits that band; reserve enough total slot memory so every returned assignment is memory-feasible. Set the cost of assigning model i to slot j on GPU g to the increase in a target pressure surrogate, using weight_i plus a congestion price proportional to size_i and the current planned residual-memory band. Add multiple slot types per GPU, including high-memory slots for large models and low-memory slots for high weight-per-size models, so the assignment can make coordinated exchanges that greedy moves cannot discover. The evaluator objective is the maximum KVPR, so costs should heavily penalize assignments that place high req_rate/slo models in the last residual-memory bands of a GPU. Keep the existing greedy placement only as a fallback if the slot construction cannot represent all models exactly. This differs from the failed MILP attempts because Hungarian assignment is a fast polynomial global matching method rather than branch-and-bound over binary placement variables.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the worst GPU KVPR by enabling coordinated global reassignment of models that are individually non-improving moves under the current greedy/local-search placement.
active_paradigms.cautions: The slot design must guarantee that summed model_size on each GPU never exceeds 80 GB; do not merely use an average slot size. linear_sum_assignment requires a square or rectangular dense cost matrix and every model needs at least one finite-cost feasible slot. Use very large finite costs rather than infinity, validate the output memory exactly, and fall back to the proven greedy placement if slot feasibility is not guaranteed.

active_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.algorithms.flow.min_cost_flow on a residual-memory state graph
active_paradigms.description: The principal weakness of the current local search is that it explores only one move or one swap per iteration, whereas KVPR often improves only after a cycle involving three or more GPUs. Construct a single min-cost-flow graph in which each GPU is represented by discrete residual-memory states, for example integer or half-GB capacity layers, and each transition that consumes a model-sized amount of memory has a cost equal to the incremental increase of a convex pressure surrogate. Send one unit of flow for every model through an assignment layer into a GPU-state path, with model-specific edges allowed only when that model fits in the relevant capacity transition. Price the final low-residual states very sharply because the true denominator is 80 minus used memory; use the model weight req_rate/slo in the transition cost so high-request models avoid crowded GPUs. A single networkx.algorithms.flow.min_cost_flow call then finds a coordinated placement under the discretized capacity model, including reassignment cycles that the incumbent's move/swap neighborhood cannot reach. The returned GPU paths can be decoded directly into placement lists, and using conservative rounded-up model sizes ensures real memory feasibility. This is structurally unlike the failed configuration MILP: it exploits the one-dimensional 80-GB resource and a polynomial network-flow solver rather than enumerating configurations or invoking integer programming repeatedly.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Attack hard instances where memory fragmentation prevents beneficial multi-GPU exchanges, while directly preserving capacity and emphasizing the maximum-pressure bottleneck.
active_paradigms.cautions: Capacity discretization must be conservative: round each model size upward and use a granularity that keeps the expanded graph small enough for evaluation time. The pressure objective is not exactly additive, so use increasing marginal costs calibrated to residual-memory bands and always calculate true KVPR after decoding. If an instance contains fractional sizes that make conservative discretization too wasteful, retain the current feasible incumbent rather than returning an infeasible flow-derived assignment.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 to build balanced pressure-profile groups before direct placement
active_paradigms.description: The existing ordering ranks models independently by their standalone pressure, which can mix large-memory models and high-request models in a way that creates denominator collapse on a few GPUs. Form a two-dimensional feature vector for every model using normalized model_size and normalized req_rate/slo, with the memory coordinate scaled strongly enough to reflect the nonlinear denominator risk. Call scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 with k equal to gpu_num to partition models into global pressure profiles, using deterministic initialization and a fixed seed for evaluator consistency. Interpret each centroid as a target GPU composition: groups with high total model size should receive relatively low total request weight, while high-weight groups should preserve more memory. Assign each cluster to one GPU and only use direct deterministic spill assignment for a cluster exceeding 80 GB, placing overflow into the cluster whose centroid and remaining capacity yield the lowest resulting true KVPR. This provides a fundamentally different basin of attraction from the incumbent greedy initialization, after which the existing move/swap cleanup can be retained if desired. It is especially useful when models naturally separate into memory-heavy/low-rate and light/high-rate populations, because good solutions deliberately counterbalance those populations rather than simply distributing standalone pressure ranks. The evaluator averages per-case maximum KVPR, so deterministic grouping avoids variance from randomized local-search restarts.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve initialization quality by balancing the joint size-versus-request composition on every GPU, reducing denominator collapse before local moves are considered.
active_paradigms.cautions: kmeans2 does not itself enforce memory capacity or minimize the exact max-ratio objective, so it must not be trusted blindly as a final placement. Standardize features robustly and use deterministic initialization; otherwise one extreme req_rate/slo model can dominate all centroids. Validate every cluster's summed size, use the current greedy solution as a safe fallback, and do not return a cluster assignment unless every GPU satisfies the 80-GB limit.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the placement globally as a set-partitioning MILP over feasible GPU configurations
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses decreasing-order greedy placement based on each model's isolated pressure, followed by at most min(16, number_of_models) best-improving single moves or pairwise swaps. Its strength is that every intermediate placement remains memory-feasible and its lexicographic sorted-pressure objective directly attacks the maximum KVPR before secondary pressures. Its main weakness is local-optimum trapping: a beneficial reassignment can require moving three or more models simultaneously, while greedy early assignments can consume the wrong memory slack. Build feasible GPU configurations: each configuration is a subset of models whose total size is below 80 GB, with its exact pressure precomputed. Use binary configuration-selection variables, require every model to occur in exactly one selected configuration, select exactly gpu_num configurations, and minimize an epigraph variable constrained to be at least the pressure of every selected configuration. This is a pure set-partitioning MILP and therefore optimizes the actual bottleneck objective globally within the enumerated configuration set, unlike surrogate load balancing. Deterministically enumerate subsets only when the instance is small enough, pruning subsets that exceed 80 GB and retaining configurations that are useful for coverage; empty configurations must be included so unused GPUs are permitted. Feed the resulting sparse constraint matrix to one MILP solve and decode selected configurations into the required placement dictionary.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The evaluator's primary quantity: the maximum exact KVPR over GPUs, while enforcing every model appears once and each selected GPU configuration fits in memory.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Full subset enumeration is exponential, so this is most suitable when evaluator instances have modest model counts; aggressively prune infeasible subsets during deterministic setup. The pressure for an empty GPU should be treated as zero, and configurations leaving zero residual memory must be excluded or assigned infinite pressure. Do not accidentally impose an at-most-one restriction on a configuration pattern if identical patterns should be usable on multiple labeled GPUs; include enough copies or use labeled configuration variables.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use direct integer-valued differential evolution on the complete model-to-GPU assignment vector
tried_paradigms.description: Represent a candidate by one integer gene per model, where gene i is its target GPU index in [0, gpu_num-1]. Evaluate a candidate by accumulating exact per-GPU model memory and weight req_rate/slo, returning the maximum weight/(80-memory) when all GPUs are feasible. Return a very large, scale-aware penalty for any memory violation, with an additional violation magnitude term so the population can move toward feasibility rather than tie on one constant penalty. Call differential evolution once with integer coordinates, a population sized relative to the number of models, and a deterministic seed; its objective is the real evaluator objective rather than the current greedy proxy. Seed one population member from the existing greedy-plus-local-search placement if the API/version permits an initial population, because that guarantees a good feasible incumbent while evolution discovers coordinated reassignment cycles. This differs fundamentally from the current move/swap descent because crossover can alter many model placements at once and can escape a no-single-swap-improvement basin. After optimization, round only if integer support is unavailable, validate capacity, and construct the placement directly from the integer vector.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact maximum KVPR, particularly instances where reducing the bottleneck needs a multi-model cyclic exchange that the 16 iterations of moves and swaps cannot reach.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use scipy's integrality support only if present in the installed version; otherwise objective-side rounding makes the landscape more discontinuous and requires a larger population. Ensure the infeasibility penalty is safely larger than every plausible feasible KVPR, but not infinite or NaN. Runtime grows with model count, so cap maxiter and use this primarily as a robust global-search alternative rather than combining it with another optimizer.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use bounded exhaustive assignment search for small instances, with the exact KVPR as the objective
tried_paradigms.description: For small model counts, encode the entire placement as a point in a gpu_num-dimensional discrete grid per model and invoke brute force directly on that assignment space. The objective must compute model memory and request-weight totals from scratch, reject assignments exceeding 80 GB, and otherwise return the exact maximum KVPR; no surrogate or greedy ordering is needed. This provides a valuable exact method because the objective is non-additive: assigning one model changes both the numerator and denominator of a GPU's pressure, so local assignment costs are not reliable. It can beat the current program on the small and medium adversarial cases where its greedy construction is trapped and its move/swap neighborhood has no improving edge. Use a deterministic pre-check on the assignment-space size and invoke exhaustive search only below a strict threshold; otherwise retain the current greedy method as the fallback. Symmetry can be reduced in deterministic setup by fixing the first model to GPU zero, because GPU labels are interchangeable, which removes a factor of gpu_num without changing the optimum. Decode the best returned coordinate vector only after rechecking feasibility and preserve all models exactly once.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact optimal maximum KVPR on small evaluator cases, improving the average score through guaranteed optimal solutions rather than heuristic local improvements.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The search space is gpu_num raised to the number of models, so it must be guarded aggressively to avoid evaluator timeouts. Invalid assignments need a finite high objective rather than exceptions, since the objective is called repeatedly. Do not use this unconditionally on large instances, and ensure the all-empty/zero-load pressure convention agrees with the evaluator's calculation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a threshold-feasibility MILP with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses decreasing single-model pressure greedy placement, followed by at most min(16,n) best-improving single moves or pair swaps. Its lexicographically sorted pressure objective is a useful tie-breaker, but it is still a shallow local search and can be trapped when improvement requires relocating several models together. Formulate the actual decision as binary assignment variables x[m,g], with every model assigned once and each GPU memory sum bounded by 80. For a fixed candidate maximum pressure T, feasibility is linear: on every GPU, sum((weight[m] + T * size[m]) * x[m,g]) must be at most 80*T. Use scipy.optimize.milp to solve this binary feasibility model, with a dense fixed grid of T values represented by threshold-selector binary variables in one MILP, or use a carefully bounded monotone threshold search if multiple calls are acceptable. Minimize the selected threshold rather than the current lexicographic surrogate, because the evaluator ultimately uses only each test case's maximum KVPR. A final placement is read directly from the integral assignment variables and therefore always respects memory constraints. This is especially promising when instances have enough models that multi-model exchanges dominate the quality gap.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct minimization of the per-test maximum KVPR, which improves the reciprocal mean score; assignment feasibility and 80 GB memory limits are enforced globally rather than repaired locally.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not use the nonlinear expression T multiplied by an unconstrained assignment sum directly in a basic MILP. Either solve linear fixed-T feasibility problems or use a finite threshold grid with proper big-M activation bounds. Set weights as req_rate/slo once, reject only genuinely infeasible instances, and use a sufficiently fine threshold grid so discretization does not erase the gain. Solver time must be capped; retain the current heuristic placement as a feasible incumbent/fallback if the MILP reaches its limit.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact subset-partition search over feasible GPU bundles via itertools.combinations
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit that the objective of a GPU depends only on the subset assigned to that GPU: its pressure is sum(weight)/ (80-sum(size)). For a candidate threshold T, enumerate model subsets that both fit in memory and satisfy their own pressure bound, then search for disjoint subsets covering all models using a bitmask partition recursion. The current greedy-plus-swap method cannot recognize a beneficial three-way or four-way rearrangement, whereas subset partitioning treats such coordinated exchanges as one decision. Generate candidate bundles with itertools.combinations, prune any subset whose memory exceeds 80 or whose pressure already exceeds T, and retain only nondominated bundles with respect to covered models and resource use. Branch on the uncovered model that has the fewest compatible bundles, which sharply reduces the partition search tree. Binary-searching or scanning candidate thresholds obtained from bundle pressures yields an exact optimum on small and medium instances. For larger instances, apply the same search only to the models on the highest-pressure GPUs after freezing clearly good bundles, making it a targeted exact large-neighborhood repair. This directly corrects the principal weakness of the incumbent: its 16 iterations and only one/two-model neighborhoods are arbitrary limits rather than consequences of the objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The maximum GPU KVPR through globally coordinated repartitioning, with particular emphasis on cases where the greedy seed requires multi-model cyclic exchanges.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is exponential in the number of models, so use bitmasks only when model count is modest and impose a node/time budget. Memoize infeasible states by (remaining-model mask, GPUs-left), and symmetry-break equivalent GPUs by requiring a canonical first model in the next selected bundle. Empty GPUs are valid and have zero pressure. For large instances, use this as an exact repair on a restricted neighborhood and preserve the incumbent if the search budget is exhausted.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use randomized multi-start greedy construction with numpy.random.Generator.permutation and best incumbent selection
tried_paradigms.description: The incumbent's initial ordering is deterministic and based on each model's isolated pressure, so one unlucky early choice can consume the specific free memory needed by a later large model. Build many diversified constructions by using numpy.random.Generator.permutation to randomize within tiers of similar size, weight, or isolated pressure, while retaining descending order between clearly different tiers. In each construction, place a model into the feasible GPU that minimizes the resulting maximum pressure, not just that target GPU's pressure; break ties by preserving the largest useful free-memory capacity. Run the existing move-and-swap descent after each construction, but score the resulting complete placement strictly by max(load/free_memory), retaining the best incumbent across restarts. Add focused restarts that place largest models first, highest weights first, and highest weight-per-memory models first, because these orderings expose different packing failures. This is fundamentally different from exact optimization: it cheaply samples many basins of attraction and lets the already-working local improvement phase polish each one. It is likely to improve average evaluator score because the evaluator averages independent test-case maxima, so avoiding a few very poor greedy seeds matters more than tiny improvements on easy cases.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Robust reduction of worst-GPU KVPR across all generated cases, especially outlier instances where the deterministic greedy seed is trapped in a poor packing basin.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a fixed seed for reproducibility and a bounded number of restarts to avoid evaluator timeout. Every randomized construction must still check remaining memory before assignment and must raise the same error only when no feasible placement exists. Compare placements using the actual scalar maximum pressure rather than only a lexicographic tuple, since the evaluator does not reward lower secondary pressures when the maximum is unchanged. Do not accept random worsening moves after local search; randomness should diversify starting packings, while incumbent replacement remains deterministic and monotone.
